title: Kabir's mother weeps
hook: in one hymn his mother cries that her son sings of the Lord instead of weaving (Gujri, Kabir)
tomorrow: The elephant that would not charge

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Weaver: the Lord who stretches out the world as warp, and your line, woven. Today the loom goes quiet, and someone notices.

The loom has stopped. In a small house in Kashi there's no clack of the shuttle today, and no cloth to take to market. There are children to feed. In the next room, a woman is crying quietly, the kind of crying that tries not to be heard. Her son, the weaver, is singing again. Not working. Singing about the Lord. The remarkable thing is who tells us this scene: Kabir himself, in a hymn in the Guru Granth Sahib. He sets his own mother's tears inside his song.
screen: `THE LOOM HAS STOPPED.` → `CHILDREN TO FEED.` → `HIS MOTHER, CRYING.`

segments.voice: The hymn is in Raag Gujri. It opens with her: Kabir's mother sobs and sobs, and asks the Lord how these children will live. Kabir, she says, has given up weaving and spinning, and written the Lord's name on his body. She isn't a villain here. She's doing the sums. A weaver who doesn't weave has no cloth, and no cloth means no food: the arithmetic of anyone lying awake over rent. Kabir doesn't mock her. He puts her tears first, before his own answer, so her side is heard first. Then he speaks. As long as he's passing thread through the bobbin, he says, he forgets the Lord he loves; the work keeps pulling his mind away. And the hymn ends with Kabir turning to her, gently: listen, my mother, the one Lord is the giver, for me and for these children too. That's the whole answer. Not, stop worrying. Not, you don't understand. Just: the same Giver holds all of us. Sikh readers hold this hymn with care. The Gurus taught honest work as part of the path, so it isn't read as permission to quit your job. It's read as a picture of a heart so full of the Name that the loom couldn't hold it, and of a son who still answers his mother tenderly. The cloth has changed, and the thread is still running.
screen: `RAAG GUJRI: HER TEARS COME FIRST.` · `SHE'S DOING THE SUMS.` · `THE BOBBIN PULLS HIS MIND AWAY.` · `ONE GIVER, FOR ALL OF US.` · then, large: `MOTHER, HE'S WEAVING LOVE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a parent, a grandparent, or whoever worried over you, and one time their worry came out sideways: a sharp word, a nagging question, a fear about your choices. Look underneath it, the way Kabir did, at what they were counting, food, safety, your future, and if forgiving feels too big today, just soften toward them by one notch. If you pray, you can hold their name with Waheguru.
Giver. Kabir's answer to his weeping mother: the one Lord is the giver, for him and for his children too.
Your line: mother, he's weaving love. Her tears came first, and his answer was gentle. Day seven hundred fifty.

howItsDone: Sikhs sing this Gujri hymn of Kabir in kirtan, and teachers often pair it with the Gurus' call to honest work, so the hymn is heard as devotion, not as a reason to stop earning.
